segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome back to Imagination Nights. [pause 3]

Settle into the bed. Pull the covers up to where you like them. [pause 8]

Take one deep breath, and let it go with a sigh. [pause 8]

Now let your breathing find its own pace. You do not have to control it. Just notice it. [pause 10]

Feel your feet getting heavy. Your legs. Your back sinking into the mattress. [pause 10]

Now let us relax the body, one part at a time. You do not have to do anything. Just notice each part as I name it, and let it get heavy. [pause 8]

Your feet. Let them be warm and heavy. [pause 15]

Your calves and your knees. Heavy. [pause 15]

Your hips and your lower back. Let them sink. [pause 15]

Your belly. Let it rise and fall on its own. [pause 15]

Your chest. Your shoulders. Your arms, all the way down to your fingertips. [pause 15]

Your neck. Your face. The little muscles around your eyes. [pause 15]

Your whole body, heavy and warm, held by the bed. [pause 15]

The day is finished. This part of the night is yours. [pause 8]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Tonight we use revision again, but on an older memory. A moment from your past that still stings when you think about it. [pause 14]

Choose something small and mild. A time you were embarrassed. A time you did not speak up. A goodbye that went badly. Please do not choose a memory of being badly hurt or abused. Those memories deserve care from a trained person, not a bedtime exercise. If one comes up, set it gently aside for now. [pause 16]

In revision, you replay the old moment in your imagination, but you let it go the way you wish it had. You are not lying to yourself about what happened. You are giving your mind a kinder picture to rest on, and practicing the person you are now. [pause 16]

This is imagination and feeling, not a promise about anything outside you. It is simply a way to set down an old weight before sleep. [pause 21]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Go back to that moment. Notice how old you were. Notice the place. [pause 31]

Let the moment begin as it began. Then, just before it went wrong, pause it. [pause 34]

Picture yourself today stepping into the scene, beside your younger self. [pause 34]

Put a hand on their shoulder. Say, I am here. We can do this differently. [pause 34]

Now let the moment play on in a new way. Hear your younger self speak up calmly. Or see the other person respond kindly. Or simply see yourself walk away with your head up. [pause 37]

Let it end gently. [pause 34]

Look at your younger self. Tell them, you did your best. I am proud of you. [pause 37]

Play the new version once more, from the start, so it becomes familiar. [pause 37]

Then let the scene fade, like a photograph left in the sun. [pause 38]

Say quietly, that is finished. I can rest. [pause 38]

Let the old weight go, and let your body be light. [pause 38]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
We will end here for tonight. [pause 10]

Keep the feeling, not the effort. Let the effort go. [pause 15]

Whatever happens tomorrow, tonight you practiced feeling at peace. That is worth something on its own. [pause 20]

Let sleep come when it comes. There is no rush. [pause 20]

Notice the weight of the covers. The cool side of the pillow. The dark. [pause 25]

Let each breath out be a little longer than the one before. [pause 25]

Nothing more to picture. Nothing more to try. Only rest. [pause 30]

Good night. [pause 60]
